1.why: All seven screens use a static, clean card layout with no moving images or pop-ups; only the technical Logs panel adds mild visual clutter.

2.why: Primary blue buttons, green status banners, and the yellow-accented help card visually stand out, though the garbled '1. 1. Request2. 2.' step list slightly muddies emphasis.

3.why: Each page presents a single labeled field and one action button, making the needed element easy to locate quickly despite the extra Logs section at the bottom.

4.why: Steps and rules are displayed on-page so little must be memorized, but the user must transcribe a 64-character token, follow a 4-part password rule, and handle a separate 6-digit code.

5.why: No password manager prompt, autofill hint, 'remember me' checkbox, or show/hide password toggle appears on any screen; all inputs are plain empty fields.

6.why: Completed steps are shown in green and issued tokens persist in the Logs panel, aiding recognition, but no saved personal items (e.g., saved email) are surfaced.

7.why: Instructions are short and plain ('Enter the six-digit safety code'), though the run-together step list and technical simulation text in Logs slightly reduce readability.

8.why: No error messages appear in any screenshot; the green banners are status confirmations, so the claim about error messages describing fixes cannot be confirmed.

9.why: No examples or placeholder text show what to type—fields are empty and instructions (e.g., 'Enter the 64-character token') give no sample format.

10.why: The system offers no choice among password, code, or face login; only a fixed password-plus-codes path exists, so such choices are neither present nor clarified.

11.why: Every step presents exactly one input and one button with no competing options, so the user is never given too many choices at once.

12.why: Each action produces a clear green outcome banner: 'Code confirmed', 'Your password has been changed', 'Signed in securely', and 'Privacy conditions accepted'.

13.why: Each step has a short instruction line, a step-specific tip banner, and a persistent 'Need help?' card, though the help content is identical on every page.

14.why: The help card promises users can pause, refresh, and return with progress saved, but no resend-code, back button, or visible error-recovery path is shown.

15.why: All seven screens repeat the identical structure—header, steps card, form card, help card, logs—so the design is highly consistent and learnable.
